about: Receiving LONG_WRITE (05-mapowanie-can.md §6) — the mechanics, on a device that has no long attribute to write: the node assembles ONE value at a time, answers once after the LAST segment with the Tid of the segments, drops a value with a gap or 100 ms of silence without a word, lets segment 0 start afresh and answers BUSY to segment 0 of a second value. The checks of 04-interakcje.md §4 run on the assembled value. What a long attribute does with it is display.json's (zadania/zrobione/FEAT-12.md).

steps.note: a scalar never travels in segments, even one that would fit (02-typy-danych.md §2.2): AutoOffTime is a u16 -> INVALID_VALUE, after the LAST segment
OnOff is read-only: access is checked before the form of the value
no endpoint 5
an element the type does not have
Device.Uid is read-only
Device.Address is a u16: a scalar in segments is a wrong value, nothing moves
segment 0 of three opens the value
segment 2 after 0: a gap — the value is dropped whole, nothing is answered (05-mapowanie-can.md §6.6)
segment 1 of the dropped value is nobody's and is ignored
a new value: segment 0
99 ms of silence — still waiting
100 ms with no next segment: dropped
the LAST segment comes too late and belongs to nothing
segment 0
segment 0 again — a retry with the same Tid starts afresh (05-mapowanie-can.md §6.5)
the LAST segment completes the retry: ONE answer
segment 0 of a value for AutoOffTime
segment 0 of a SECOND value while the first is open: BUSY at once, the first goes on (05-mapowanie-can.md §6.7)
the second value's LAST segment has no assembly and is ignored
the first completes as if nothing happened
segments to another node are not ours
a segment shorter than its two header bytes is broken and ignored
an ordinary write still works next to all this
